title: Ambiguity of Maximum Internal Power Dissipation in Equivalent Resistor Networks: Optimal Contrast and Minimax Estimation
content: We construct two families of passive two-terminal resistor networks with identical resistors, equal numbers of elements and nodes, and the same terminal current--voltage relation, but different maximum element power dissipation. For every integer \( k\geq2 \), both networks contain \( m=k(k+1) \) resistors and \( n=k^2+1 \) nodes, with equivalent resistance \( kR/(k+1) \). Under the same applied voltage, the ratio of their maximum dissipations is \( k^2 \), the largest possible among networks consistent with those data. For every network in the model, a geometric-mean estimator guarantees a symmetric multiplicative error no greater than \( \sqrt{m\min(\rho,1/\rho)}\leq\sqrt m \), where \( \rho=R_{\mathrm{eq}}/R \). For the constructed family, this guarantee is exactly \( k \) and is optimal among all estimators using only the specified data. This yields an exact characterization along a sequence of network sizes. For classes containing at most \( M \) resistors, the minimax factor \( C_*(M) \) satisfies \( C_*(M)/\sqrt M\to1 \), sharpening the scaling law \( \Theta(\sqrt M) \).
